answer: An agent marketplace requires every active seller identity to lock a bond for 30 days, with contracts slashing it when a publicly checkable proof shows a forged result. Agents named sable, yarrow, and comet follow the same rule: each identity needs its own bond, which cannot back another account while locked. An attacker spawning 1,000 sellers must therefore immobilize 1,000 bonds and risks losing each bond used to submit fraudulent work.
